simple: CSS is the language websites use to decide how things look. This page shows how each CSS idea matches a Roblox UI styling idea, with side-by-side examples. Even if you have never written CSS, it is a handy tour of every kind of selector, plus hover effects, rounded corners, screen-size rules, variables, and smooth transitions. Each example is a short LocalScript you can paste and try.
analogy: It is like a phrasebook between two languages: "button" in CSS is `"TextButton"` in Roblox, ".class" in CSS is a tag in Roblox, and so on.
keyPoints: To test, put a `StyleSheet` in ReplicatedStorage, and a `ScreenGui` in StarterGui with a `LocalScript` and a `StyleLink` inside it.

Class selectors like `"TextButton"` match every object of that class. Tag selectors like `".ButtonPrimary"` match tagged objects. Name selectors like `"#ModalFrame"` match by `Name`, and names do not have to be unique.
`>` means direct child, and `>>` means any descendant (child, grandchild, and so on). Commas list several selectors that share the same properties.
State selectors like `"ImageLabel:Hover"` apply only while that state is active, like the mouse being over it.
`::UICorner` style selectors add phantom modifiers, for example rounded corners on every Frame tagged `RoundedCorner20`.
Queries use `@`. Built-in ones like `@ViewportDisplaySizeSmall` or `@ReducedMotionEnabledTrue` need no setup; custom ones use a `::StyleQuery` rule with a condition like `MinSize`.
Variables are tokens: set an attribute on the sheet, then use it with `$`, like `"$ButtonBgColor"`.
`SetPropertyTransitions()` makes changes animate smoothly, and rules can be nested inside other rules so their selectors merge.

terms.CSS: The style language for websites. Roblox styling borrows many of its ideas.
terms.selector: Text that picks which objects a rule changes, like `"TextButton"` or `".MenuContainer > TextButton"`.
terms.combinator: A symbol that joins selectors to describe family relationships, like `>` for child or `>>` for descendant.
terms.child: An object directly inside another. If a button is inside MenuFrame, it is MenuFrame's child.
terms.descendant: Any object inside another at any depth. A button inside a sub-frame inside MenuFrame is a descendant of MenuFrame but not its child.
terms.pseudo-class: In CSS, a state like hover. In Roblox, a state selector such as `:Hover` or `:Press`.
terms.pseudo-instance: A phantom object a rule adds, like `::UICorner` giving every match rounded corners of 20 pixels.
terms.container query: A rule that depends on the size of a parent. Example: only when the parent Frame is at least 400 pixels wide, make the button red.
terms.media query: A rule that depends on the device or settings, like small screen, touch input, or reduced motion.
terms.AbsoluteSize: The real size of a UI object in pixels on screen right now. `MinSize` queries check this.
terms.reduced motion: A player setting asking for less animation. `@ReducedMotionEnabledTrue` lets you respect it.
terms.transition: Animating from one value to another over time, like rotating to -5 degrees over 1.25 seconds instead of instantly.
terms.nesting: Putting a rule inside another rule. A `"> TextButton"` rule inside a `"#MenuFrame"` rule means buttons that are children of MenuFrame.

example.title: Buttons that tilt smoothly on hover
example.place: LocalScript inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui (with a StyleLink in the ScreenGui and a StyleSheet in ReplicatedStorage)
example.code:
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local coreSheet = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("StyleSheet")
local screenGui = script.Parent
local styleLink = screenGui:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("StyleLink")
styleLink.StyleSheet = coreSheet

-- Normal look for every TextButton
local buttonRule = Instance.new("StyleRule")
buttonRule.Selector = "TextButton"
buttonRule:SetProperties({
	BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromHex("335FFF"),
	TextColor3 = Color3.fromHex("E1E1E1"),
	Size = UDim2.new(0.15, 0, 0, 40),
	BorderSizePixel = 0,
})
-- Animate color and rotation changes instead of jumping
buttonRule:SetPropertyTransitions({
	BackgroundColor3 = TweenInfo.new(1, Enum.EasingStyle.Cubic, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
	Rotation = TweenInfo.new(1.25, Enum.EasingStyle.Cubic, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
})
buttonRule.Parent = coreSheet

-- Look while the mouse is over a TextButton
local hoverRule = Instance.new("StyleRule")
hoverRule.Selector = "TextButton:Hover"
hoverRule:SetProperties({
	AutoButtonColor = false,
	BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromHex("33AAFF"),
	Rotation = -5,
})
hoverRule.Parent = coreSheet

-- Create a button to see it work
local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
button.Text = "Main Menu"
button.Parent = screenGui
explain: The first lines find the StyleSheet and connect it to this ScreenGui through the StyleLink.
`buttonRule` gives every TextButton a blue background, light text, and a size of 15% of the screen wide by 40 pixels tall.
`SetPropertyTransitions` says color changes take 1 second and rotation changes take 1.25 seconds, slowing down at the end.
`hoverRule` uses `:Hover`, so it only applies while the mouse is over the button: lighter blue and tilted -5 degrees.
Because of the transitions, the button smoothly tilts and brightens when you hover, and smoothly goes back when you leave.

watchOut: Mixing up `>` and `>>`. `>` only matches direct children; use `>>` if the object might be deeper inside.
Writing CSS-style descendant selectors with a space, like `".MenuContainer TextButton"`. Roblox uses `>>` for that.
Forgetting to tag objects for tag selectors. `CollectionService:AddTag(button, "ButtonPrimary")` must run, or the `.ButtonPrimary` rule matches nothing.
Thinking `#Name` must be unique like a web id. In Roblox, every object with that name matches.
Leaving `AutoButtonColor` on when styling hover colors. Set it to `false` so your hover color shows.
